correctness.rationale: Ehrenborg–Hetyei prove the exhaustive dichotomy for forest independence complexes; the explicitly checked exact pair recurrence has a 3- or 6-state period, identifying contractibility. Direct dominating-level and separated-neighborhood witnesses give \(\gamma=|P|\), and Marietti–Testa identify sphere degree \(\gamma-1\). The augmented chain Hopf trace is \(-Z_g\), giving degree \(Z_g/Z_{\mathrm{id}}\). For each branch-swap generator the cycle quotient is a rooted tree with \(b-1\) branches locally; its state pair differs by scalar \(\lambda\) and propagation preserves that scalar to the root. The scalar equals the sign of the induced block swap on \(P\). Generators span the full rooted automorphism group. No unproved infinite search or finite-field homology assumption enters the proof. Two ordinary Python 3 checkers reproduce 2700 exact recurrence cases and independent simplicial traces/boundary ranks for 17 small generator cases; they are corroborative not a substitute for the exact argument.

value.rationale: The complete rooted tree is a natural family of graph complexes with a large canonical iterated-wreath-product symmetry group. Earlier work determines homotopy type, but whether each rooted automorphism preserves or reverses the generator of integral top homology is not encoded by that nonequivariant classification. The formula identifies the complete, often nontrivial orientation character across the infinite family and specifies which local generators reverse orientation. This is an intrinsic equivariant invariant, not an arbitrary finite computation, a parameter substitution or a recomputation of known Betti numbers. No equivariant homotopy classification is claimed.
